close_lag_1_lt_3.label: Close t-1 < t-3
close_lag_1_lt_3.desc: Checks whether close price at t-1 is lower than at t-3
close_lag_1_lt_3.help: A basic lag comparison filter: compare two past close points without using moving averages.
close_lag_1_lt_3.whenToUse: Is short-term price momentum weakening? Use this for momentum slowdown or pullback setups; in practice it is often paired with trend-following filters similar to post-momentum checks discussed in momentum literature.
close_lag_1_lt_3.howToRead: Example: left_lag=1, right_lag=3, operator=lt means yesterday's close must be below the close three sessions ago. Increasing right_lag compares against older history (more structural), while decreasing it makes the signal more reactive. In fast-growth sectors this can trigger frequently, while defensives may show slower transitions.
close_lag_1_lt_3.caution: A single lag comparison can create many false signals in choppy markets. Combine with volume/trend filters (e.g., volume above average, MA alignment). Sector behavior differs, and corporate events or delayed/adjusted price data can distort isolated comparisons.

return_turnaround.label: Return Turnaround
return_turnaround.desc: Prev N-day return <= threshold and recent N-day return >= threshold
return_turnaround.help: Finds reversal setups where prior returns were weak, then recent returns turned positive.

min_volume.label: Min Volume
min_volume.help: Ensures enough daily volume so you can buy and sell easily.

volume_above_avg.label: Volume Above Avg
volume_above_avg.help: Spots stocks with higher-than-usual trading activity — may signal growing interest.

volume_spike.label: Volume Spike
volume_spike.help: Detects sudden surges in volume, often preceding big price moves.

ma_touch.label: MA Touch
ma_touch.help: Price is touching a key moving average — a potential support or bounce point.

above_ma.label: Above MA
above_ma.help: Stock is trading above its moving average, suggesting an uptrend.

below_ma.label: Below MA
below_ma.help: Stock is trading below its moving average, suggesting a downtrend or value zone.

ma_cross_up.label: MA Cross Up
ma_cross_up.help: Golden Cross: short-term MA crosses above long-term MA — a classic bullish signal.

ma_cross_down.label: MA Cross Down
ma_cross_down.help: Death Cross: short-term MA crosses below long-term MA — a classic bearish signal.

rsi_oversold.label: RSI Oversold
rsi_oversold.help: RSI is low — the stock may be oversold and due for a bounce.
rsi_oversold.whenToUse: Use for mean-reversion setups after sharp pullbacks.
rsi_oversold.howToRead: Lower RSI means stronger oversold signal. Typical references are around 30.
rsi_oversold.caution: In strong downtrends RSI can stay oversold for extended periods.

rsi_overbought.label: RSI Overbought
rsi_overbought.help: RSI is high — the stock may be overbought and due for a pullback.
rsi_overbought.whenToUse: Use for pullback-risk checks or short-term contrarian setups.
rsi_overbought.howToRead: Higher RSI means stronger overbought signal. Typical references are around 70.
rsi_overbought.caution: In strong uptrends RSI can stay overbought longer than expected.

rsi_range.label: RSI Range
rsi_range.help: RSI is within a neutral zone — useful for finding stable momentum.
rsi_range.whenToUse: Use when you want stable momentum names within a controlled RSI band.
rsi_range.howToRead: Only stocks inside the lower-upper RSI band pass.
rsi_range.caution: Too narrow a range can overfit and reduce candidate diversity.

bollinger_width.label: Bollinger Width
bollinger_width.help: Bollinger Bands are narrow, signaling low volatility — a big move may follow.

volume_below_avg.label: Volume Below Avg
volume_below_avg.help: Volume is unusually low — the stock is in a quiet accumulation phase.

price_flat.label: Price Flat

obv_trend.label: OBV Trend

stochastic_divergence.label: Stochastic Divergence

vpci_divergence.label: VPCI Divergence

day_of_week_seasonality.label: Day-of-Week Seasonality
day_of_week_seasonality.desc: Filters stocks that historically perform better on a selected weekday.
day_of_week_seasonality.help: Looks for repeatable weekday return patterns in historical data.
day_of_week_seasonality.whenToUse: Use for short-horizon tactical entries when you suspect weekday effects in your market.
day_of_week_seasonality.howToRead: A higher minimum average return is stricter. Start small and verify persistence by period.
day_of_week_seasonality.caution: Weekday effects can disappear after transaction costs or regime shifts; validate out-of-sample.

net_share_issuance_filter.label: Net Share Issuance Filter
net_share_issuance_filter.desc: Limits dilution by filtering companies issuing too many new shares.
net_share_issuance_filter.help: Keeps companies with controlled net share issuance.
net_share_issuance_filter.whenToUse: Use in quality/value screens to avoid dilution-heavy names.
net_share_issuance_filter.howToRead: This is a max threshold: lower values imply less shareholder dilution.
net_share_issuance_filter.caution: Temporary issuance can be strategic (M&A/capex); review context before excluding.

insider_net_buying.label: Insider Net Buying
insider_net_buying.help: Filters stocks based on Insider Net Buying threshold settings.

short_float_pct_filter.label: Short Float % Filter
short_float_pct_filter.desc: Limits candidates by short interest as a percentage of float.
short_float_pct_filter.help: Keeps stocks where short float is below your risk tolerance.
short_float_pct_filter.whenToUse: Use to avoid crowded short names in long strategies, or invert logic in squeeze-focused setups.
short_float_pct_filter.howToRead: This is a max threshold: lower values mean lower shorting pressure and usually lower squeeze risk.
short_float_pct_filter.caution: High short float is not always bearish; it can also fuel sharp squeezes.

short_interest_ratio_filter.label: Short Interest Ratio Filter
short_interest_ratio_filter.desc: Filters by days-to-cover level from short interest.
short_interest_ratio_filter.help: Controls exposure to names with heavy short positioning relative to volume.
short_interest_ratio_filter.whenToUse: Use with liquidity filters to avoid hard-to-exit names.
short_interest_ratio_filter.howToRead: This is a max threshold: lower is generally safer for execution.
short_interest_ratio_filter.caution: Low volume periods can inflate days-to-cover temporarily.

earnings_surprise_filter.label: Earnings Surprise Filter
earnings_surprise_filter.desc: Filters stocks with positive earnings surprise vs consensus.
earnings_surprise_filter.help: Finds names that beat expectations by at least your threshold.
earnings_surprise_filter.whenToUse: Use around earnings seasons for momentum continuation or post-event drift ideas.
earnings_surprise_filter.howToRead: This is a min threshold: higher values demand stronger positive surprise.
earnings_surprise_filter.caution: One-off accounting effects can distort surprise; confirm with guidance/revision metrics.
